text:
alex: Quick check — we still have ambiguity between the loader's "index-first" verification and the runtime's soft-verify path. observed a prod spike where a malformed safetensors chunk caused repeated fallback thrashing. anyone seen similar?
mina: saw that at ~03:10 UTC yesterday. runtime retried streaming fallback 4x, then OOMed while trying to rehydrate prefix cache. Noticed manifest says chunk-size 4MB but actual blob had 4.2MB.
jon: ouch. is that a checksum vs size mismatch or a streaming-chunk framing bug?
sara: size mismatch likely. surfacing the error looked like this in the logs: 
```
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z loader: shard read failed: expected 4194304 bytes, got 4404019
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z runtime: fallback -> stream-merge candidate selected
2026-03-20T03:10:12Z cache: eviction triggered during rehydrate, free=120MB
```
jon: given that, i think we need two things: a clearer contract for partial reads (who verifies length / checksum) and a lightweight hint API from the serving runtime to the loader about warmup priority.
alex: +1. proposal: introduce a Warmup-Hint header/attribute that is advisory (runtime -> loader) and a strict ManifestSanity step (loader/internal) that fails fast for checksum mismatch. If manifest sanity fails, runtime should fall back to a compatible (older) bundle, not retry streaming same shard.
mina: i like advisory hints. we should avoid coupling to HTTP headers only — internal IPC + sidecar protocols should carry same schema. suggestion proto: 
```
WarmupHint {
  shard_id: string
  priority: int // 0 low, 1 normal, 2 hot
  verify_mode: "fast" | "full" // fast = length+crc32, full = blake3
  prefetch_window_ms: int
}
```
alex: semantics: verify_mode tells loader how aggressively to validate before returning a memory-mapped view. fast for immediate starts, full for scheduled background hydration. runtime can downgrade verify_mode if it sees repeated latency.
jon: tradeoffs: fast verify avoids tail latency but lets corrupt payload through. full verify increases start latency and may double read bandwidth. we need a telemetry signal to drive policy. propose metrics: shard_verify_mode, shard_verify_failures, shard_stream_retries, warmup_priority_latency.
sara: ops ask: what happens on mismatch? do we remove bundle from rotation? revert to previous commit? we discussed auto-rollbacks earlier, but need to codify.
mina: concrete safe policy: on checksum fail during full verify -> mark bundle degraded, route new requests to previous pinned version for 5 minutes and emit alert. on fast verify fail -> try fallback streaming once, if streaming checksum mismatch too -> mark degraded.
alex: also want to avoid noisy pager for transient network blips. make degradation threshold = 3 distinct hosts failing same shard within 10m.
jon: implementation note: exposing verify_mode in the manifest could be useful: model bundle authors can mark shards as expensive-to-verify (e.g., quantized delta shards) and runtime can choose. but manifests are signed, so we need careful schema versioning.
sara: ops + security: signed manifest + per-shard blake3 checksum still required. verify_mode is just which checks to run synchronously.
mina: small perf sketch: full blake3 verify over 200MB shard ~ 150ms on p4d local NVMe, cf. mmap + on-demand page-in will still page faults. So full verify cost is non-trivial.
alex: question: should loader ever return a zero-copy mmap if fast verify passes but full verify fails later? that would risk corrupt tensors being used. Maybe return read-only copy-on-write buffer for fast mode?
jon: copy-on-write costs memory. alternate: return mmap view but mark kv-cache invalid until full verify completes; runtime must be able to detect incomplete-verify state and avoid using those tensors for long-latency-critical work (lower priority requests). adds complexity.
sara: preference: simpler first pass: warmup-hint + fast verify returns a guarded mmap and runtime tags requests as low-priority until bundle is fully verified. we'll iterate on COW if memory pressure proves too high.
mina: +1. Also add a small bounded retry fence in loader to avoid repeated identical reads: if same host is currently verifying shard X, subsequent requests wait up to 200ms for result instead of triggering parallel downloads. reduces thundering herd.
alex: i can draft an RFC for the Warmup-Hint wire schema + manifest flag + degradation policy. will include metrics and alert thresholds. anyone want to pair on the perf numbers section?
jon: happy to. can pull benchmarks for blake3 vs crc32 and COW memory overhead.
sara: ops team wants rollback playbook; i'll write the runbook appendix (who to notify, how to pin previous bundle, scripts).
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: please add migration test to loader integration suite: simulate corrupted chunk, confirm degraded marking, ensure runtime routes to fallback.
mina: one more thought — for private deployments (on-prem), customers may disable full verify for performance. need config knob and clear warning in console.
alex: noted. RFC will include knob + warning text. thanks all, will post draft by EOD. :thumbsup:
